items.title: No local estimate of the plan completeness and revisit association
items.whyItMatters: The funding decision for an electronic plan rests on whether completeness matters in this population, and the only comparable cohort comes from another province and template.
items.opportunity: Estimate the adjusted association in 2022 to 2025 discharges with linked revisits.

items.title: Revisits elsewhere are invisible without linkage
items.whyItMatters: One fifth of revisits happen at other hospitals (claim c2), more for lower-income families, so hospital-only data would bias the comparison.
items.opportunity: Use the provincial emergency visits dataset as the outcome source and report how many events came from other hospitals.

items.title: Confounding by severity and engagement
items.whyItMatters: Children who receive complete plans may differ in severity and family engagement (claim c5).
items.opportunity: Pre-specify the adjustment set and add injury visits as a negative control outcome.

items.title: Plans that are complete but not understood
items.whyItMatters: Caregivers who prefer another language understood English plans less well (claim c4).
items.opportunity: Record language preference and interpreter use and report the association by language group.

items.title: Illegible handwritten doses
items.whyItMatters: The yellow-zone item had the lowest agreement because doses were illegible (claim c3).
items.opportunity: Score an illegible dose as missing and double-score a random 10 percent of plans.

errorsFound: The need treats a complete plan as a cause of fewer revisits; the retrieved evidence supports an association that may partly reflect severity and engagement.
reevaluation: The gaps confirm a linked cohort with a pre-specified adjustment set, a negative control outcome and reporting by language group; the linkage is essential rather than optional.
summary: Five gaps; the missing local estimate, invisible revisits and confounding are high severity.
